He played [[college basketball]] for the [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]] before being drafted 15th overall, after his freshman season, in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. Harkless has represented the [[Puerto Rico men's national basketball team|Puerto Rican national team]] internationally. ==High school career== Harkless was born and adopted in [[New York City]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/players/maurice/harkless/203090|title=Maurice Harkless stats, details, videos, and news|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 23, 2017}} He attended [[Forest Hills High School (New York)|Forest Hills High School]] in [[Queens]], before transferring to [[South Kent School]] in [[Connecticut]] prior to his senior season. He earned all-metro honors from both the ''[[Chicago Daily News]]'' and ''[[New York Post]]'' in 2008–09 and 2009–10, in addition to being named the ''New York Daily News'''s Queens High School Player of the Year in 2009–10 after averaging 16.5 points and 11.5 rebounds.{{cite web|url=http://www.redstormsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/harkless_moe00.html|title=Maurice Harkless Bio|work=redstormsports.com|access-date=December 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180507002020/http://www.redstormsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/harkless_moe00.html|archive-date=May 7, 2018|url-status=dead}} At South Kent in 2010–11, he averaged 27.2 points, 13.6 rebounds, 4.2 assists, 3.1 blocks, and 1.6 steals per game. He was named MVP at the 2011 Yo Mama Classic in Philadelphia. ==College career== [[File:Moe Harkless.jpg|right|thumb|Harkless during his lone season at [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]]|216x216px]] Harkless played and started all 32 games during his freshman season at [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's University]] in 2011–12, averaging 15.5 points, 8.6 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 1.59 steals, and 1.41 blocks in 36.1 minutes per game. He led the Red Storm in rebounding, blocked shots and minutes played, while finishing second in scoring and steals. He ranked second in the nation among freshmen in rebounding and sixth in scoring. He was named the [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|Big East Rookie of the Year]] and earned All-Big East Honorable Mention. He scored in double figures 26 times and had 20-plus points seven times, including a career-high 32 points against [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]] on December 27. He also recorded 11 double-doubles. In March 2012, Harkless declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite web|last=Darcy|first=Kieran|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/ncb/story/_/id/7654238/moe-harkless-st-john-red-storm-consider-entering-nba-draft|title=Moe Harkless to consider NBA draft|work=ESPN.com|date=March 7, 2012|access-date=December 23, 2017}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/story/_/id/7709890/moe-harkless-leaving-st-john-red-storm-early-nba-draft|title=Moe Harkless leaving for NBA draft|work=ESPN.com|date=March 20, 2012|access-date=December 23, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Orlando Magic (2012–2015)=== [[File:Maurice Harkless, Washington at Orlando 085.jpg|right|thumb|Harkless with the Magic in December 2012]] On June 28, 2012, Harkless was selected with the 15th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. On August 10, 2012, he was traded from Philadelphia to the [[Orlando Magic]] as part of a four-team, 12-player deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/08/10/dwight-howard-trade.ap/index.html |title=It's official: Howard dealt to Lakers in four-team trade |work=NBA.com |date=August 10, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120811080542/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/08/10/dwight-howard-trade.ap/index.html |archive-date=August 11, 2012}} Harkless impressed in his first NBA season, averaging 8.2 points per game and providing good defense.{{cite web|last=Goldberg|first=Wes|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1906433-should-mo-harkless-still-be-a-part-of-orlando-magics-future|title=Should Maurice Harkless Still Be a Part of Orlando Magic's Future?|work=bleacherreport.com|date=January 3, 2014|access-date=December 23, 2017}} He scored in double figures 29 times and had 20-plus points four times, including a career-high 28 points on April 1 against the [[Houston Rockets]]. He recorded one double-double during the season, registering 19 points and a career-high 14 rebounds on February 2 against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He had at least one steal in 50 games and two-or-more steals 22 times, including a career-high six steals on March 15 against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. Harkless began the [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14 season]] starting alongside [[Arron Afflalo]] and [[Jameer Nelson]]. When [[Victor Oladipo]] was inserted into the starting lineup, coach [[Jacque Vaughn]] opted to play combinations of Nelson, Oladipo, Afflalo and [[Tobias Harris]] on the wing. As a result of the backlogged situation, Harkless' minutes decreased from his rookie season. He scored in double figures 30 times and had 20+ points three times, including a season-high 22 points on January 6 against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and February 25 against the [[Washington Wizards]]. He had one double-double during the season, recording 12 points and a season-high 10 rebounds on March 8 against the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. He recorded at least one steal 54 times and had two-or-more steals 31 times, including a season-high five steals on March 5 against Houston. During the 2013–14 season, Harkless averaged 7.4 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 1.0 assists in 24.4 minutes per game. He improved his 3-point shooting, increasing his accuracy from 27.4 percent as a rookie to 38.3 percent in his second year.{{cite web|last=Robbins|first=Josh|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/magic-basketblog/os-mbb-maurice-harkless-puerto-rico-20140729-post.html|title=Maurice Harkless won't play for Puerto Rico's national team this summer|work=orlandosentinel.com|date=July 29, 2014|access-date=December 23, 2017}} Harkless bottomed out in [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15]], receiving minimal playing time and creating questions about his future.{{cite web|last=Schmitz|first=Brian|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/magic-basketblog/os-evalutating-orlando-magic-maurice-harkless-201415-season-20150513-post.html|title=Evaluating Maurice Harkless' 2014-15 season|work=orlandosentinel.com|date=May 13, 2015|access-date=December 23, 2017}} He played in only a career-low 45 games during his third season in Orlando despite good health. Harkless sat behind fellow forwards Tobias Harris and [[Aaron Gordon]] during the 2014–15 season and averaged just 15 minutes per game. On March 18 against the [[Dallas Mavericks]], Harkless started for Harris and played 36 minutes. He scored 18 points on 8-of-15 shooting, including two 3-pointers, grabbed six rebounds and recorded four steals. In the next game however against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], Harkless missed five of six shots and finished with just two points in 28 minutes. He made little impact the rest of the season. ===Portland Trail Blazers (2015–2019)=== On July 14, 2015, Harkless was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for a 2020 second round draft pick.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-maurice-harkless-orlando|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Maurice Harkless from Orlando|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2015|access-date=July 14, 2015}} He worked his way up from the end of the bench to starter by the end of the 2015–16 season. Portland began to play small late in the season by inserting Harkless into the lineup. After averaging 6.4 points and 3.6 rebounds a game during the regular season, Harkless rode his inspired play into the playoffs, boosting his numbers to 11 points and 5.1 rebounds respectively.{{cite web|last=Gordon|first=Spencer|url=https://ripcityproject.com/2016/05/25/blazers-review-harkless/|title=Blazers Review: Maurice Harkless|work=ripcityproject.com|date=May 25, 2016|access-date=December 23, 2017}} On February 10, 2016, he set season highs with 19 points and 13 rebounds in a 116–103 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160210/HOUPOR/gameinfo.html|title=Lillard scores 31 as surging Blazers beat Rockets 116-103|work=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2016|access-date=February 10, 2016}} On April 5, 2016, he recorded a season-high 20 points and a career-high 16 rebounds in a 115–107 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160405/PORSAC/gameinfo.html|title=McCollum has 30 as Trail Blazers beat Kings 115-107|work=NBA.com|date=April 5, 2016|access-date=April 6, 2016}} A [[restricted free agent]] over the summer, Harkless was expected to be re-signed, but when the Trail Blazers added [[Evan Turner]] and reacquired [[Allen Crabbe]], it appeared Harkless would be heading elsewhere.{{cite web|last=Sampson|first=Peter|url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2017/5/9/15574666/maurice-harkless-2016-17-nba-season-review-portland-trail-blazers|title=Maurice Harkless 2016-17 NBA Season in Review|work=blazersedge.com|date=May 9, 2017|access-date=December 23, 2017}} However, on July 27, 2016,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-re-sign-forward-maurice-harkless|title=TRAIL BLAZERS RE-SIGN FORWARD MAURICE HARKLESS|work=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2016|access-date=July 27, 2016}} Harkless signed a four-year, $40 million contract to remain with the team. After experimenting with various lineups early in the preseason, coach [[Terry Stotts]] quickly settled back on Harkless as the starting small forward, a position he would hold on to for the majority of the season. After a scoreless, single-rebound performance on opening night against the [[Utah Jazz]], Harkless put up 23 points and eight rebounds in the second game of the season against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on October 27. Harkless scored a season high-tying 23 points on November 30 against the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/harklma01/gamelog/2017/|title=Maurice Harkless 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 23, 2017}} Harkless improved his 3-point shooting during the 2016–17 season, increasing his average from 28 percent to 35 percent. It was reported that Harkless was due a $500,000 bonus if he shot 35 percent or better from the 3-point line. Sitting at .351 with four games to go, Harkless declined to attempt a 3-pointer for the rest of the season, even sitting out one of the four games for unrelated reasons. Harkless started the [[2017–18 NBA season|2017–18 season]] as the starting small forward, before losing the spot after averaging 4.5 points and 3.8 rebounds over his first 18 games.{{cite web|last=Simms|first=Raymond|url=https://hoopshabit.com/2018/05/17/portland-trail-blazers-2017-18-player-grades-maurice-harkless/|title=Portland Trail Blazers: 2017-18 player grades for Maurice Harkless|work=hoopshabit.com|date=May 17, 2018|access-date=January 10, 2018}} On December 23, he scored a season-high 22 points against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/harklma01/gamelog/2018/|title=Maurice Harkless 2017-18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 10, 2018}} He found himself in and out of the rotation until an injury to [[Evan Turner]] in February saw Harkless return to the starting line-up. He appeared in 59 games in 2017–18 after surgery in late March to his left knee saw him sit out the last nine games of the regular season and two of Portland's four playoff games. Over the first half of the [[2018–19 NBA season|2018–19 season]], Harkless missed 14 games because of his troublesome left knee.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071291|title=McCollum scores 24 points, Trail Blazers beat Bulls 124-112|work=ESPN.com|date=January 9, 2019|access-date=January 10, 2019|quote=Harkless, who had surgery on the knee last March, has missed 14 games this season because of the knee.}} On April 9, 2019, he scored 26 points and hit a corner 3-pointer at the buzzer to lift the Trail Blazers to a 104–101 win over the Lakers.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071892|title=Harkless' 3 sends Blazers past LA 104-101 after Magic quits|work=ESPN.com|date=April 9, 2019|access-date=April 10, 2019}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2019–2020)=== On July 6, 2019, Harkless was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] along with a protected first round pick from the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] as part of a four-team trade, in which Miami acquired [[Jimmy Butler]] and the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] acquired [[Hassan Whiteside]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/harkless-prep|title=L.A. ==Personal life== Harkless is the son of Rosa Harkless. He has one sister, Shakima Harkless, and a brother, Tyler Rodgers. His maternal grandfather is from Puerto Rico.{{cite web|last=Henson|first=Joaquin M.|url=http://www.philstar.com/sports/2014/04/23/1315080/puerto-rico-beatable|title=Is Puerto Rico beatable?|work=philstar.com|date=April 23, 2014|access-date=December 23, 2017}} He was raised by grandmother Barbara Harkless. ==See also== * [[List of Puerto Ricans]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{commons category}} {{basketballstats |nba=203090 |bbr=h/harklma01}} * [https://web.archive.org/web/20180507002020/http://www.redstormsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/harkless_moe00.html St. John's Red Storm bio] {{2012 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Harkless, Maurice}} [[Category:1993 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:American people of Puerto Rican descent]] [[Category:Sportspeople of Puerto Rican descent]] [[Category:Basketball players from New York City]] [[Category:Forest Hills High School (New York) alumni]] [[Category:Los Angeles Clippers players]] [[Category:Miami Heat players]] [[Category:New York Knicks players]] [[Category:Orlando Magic players]] [[Category:Philadelphia 76ers draft picks]] [[Category:Portland Trail Blazers players]] [[Category:Puerto Rican men's basketball players]] [[Category:21st-century Puerto Rican sportsmen]] [[Category:Rip City Remix players]] [[Category:Sacramento Kings players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:South Kent School alumni]] [[Category:St. John's Red Storm men's basketball players]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]]
